creator: Martin Scorsese
geocode_query: Columbus Avenue and West 88th Street, Manhattan
notes: A condemned tenement on the west side of Columbus Avenue between West 88th and 89th Streets; Travis's apartment and the brothel interiors were built inside it. Identified from a 1975 call sheet. Demolished; a large apartment building replaced the block in 1985, so the old street number may not geocode.
source_quote: The production sheet substantiated that the address was 586 Columbus Avenue
source2_quote: Different interiors within same building: Travis' apartment; bloodbath sequence; and Iris' room. Original building since demolished.

creator: Delbert Mann
address_as_given: on the other side of Webster Avenue
notes: Dialogue puts the house 'on the other side of Webster Avenue'; the walk home was shot on the Grand Concourse at 3050 (shot mirror-reversed), so placed just east of Webster Avenue near Bedford Park Boulevard. The house interior was likely a Hollywood soundstage (Samuel Goldwyn Studios). A reader comment on nycinfilm reports house number 2454 on screen, unverified.
source_quote: The couple quietly strolls back to Marty’s home (which is “on the other side of Webster Avenue”), passing 3050 Grand Concourse.
source2_quote: Marty Piletti is an Italian-American butcher who lives in The Bronx with his widowed mother.

creator: Spike Lee
address_as_given: a loft underneath the Brooklyn Bridge
notes: Sources disagree: Nelson George, a friend of Lee who saw an early cut, puts her loft under the Brooklyn Bridge, while contemporary reviews (Harvard Crimson) and most writing place Nola in Fort Greene, where much of the film was shot. No street address found.
source_quote: Nola is a boho graphic artist with three boyfriends who lives in a loft underneath the Brooklyn Bridge.
source2_quote: a seriously sexy young woman taking good care of herself in Fort Greene, Brooklyn

creator: Hal Ashby
address_as_given: an inner-city tenement in Park Slope
notes: Elgar buys the building intending to make it his home and stays on as landlord among the tenants. The dialogue names Park Slope; no story address found, so placed at the filmed block on Prospect Place. The source novel by Kristin Hunter was not set in Brooklyn.
